title: Microsoft 365 Backup: Full Workload Backup policies for SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap, the supplied Microsoft notice and Microsoft Learn. Its configuration paths, automation, consumption pricing and revised rollout dates match the sources checked.

claims.claim: Full Workload Backup allows an administrator to protect an entire SharePoint, OneDrive or Exchange workload with a single policy.
claims.quote: allows admins to quickly protect an entire workload (SharePoint, OneDrive, or Exchange) with a single policy

claims.claim: Full-workload coverage operates across the tenant.
claims.quote: Automatically backup all Exchange or OneDrive users and/or SharePoint sites in the tenant

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The policy automatically protects eligible SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts and Exchange mailboxes without individual selection.
claims.quote: Full Workload Backup provides automatic protection for all eligible SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts, or Exchange mailboxes in your organization that aren't already protected by another backup policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters
claims.claim: Items included in a custom policy are outside Full Workload Backup's protection scope.
claims.quote: Full Workload Backup automatically protects all eligible protection units that aren't already included in a custom backup policy, added to the exclusion list, or in the process of being permanently deleted from Microsoft 365 Backup.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters
claims.claim: Items on the exclusion list are outside Full Workload Backup's protection scope.
claims.quote: Full Workload Backup automatically protects all eligible protection units that aren't already included in a custom backup policy, added to the exclusion list, or in the process of being permanently deleted from Microsoft 365 Backup.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Items being permanently deleted from Microsoft 365 Backup are outside Full Workload Backup's protection scope.
claims.quote: Full Workload Backup automatically protects all eligible protection units that aren't already included in a custom backup policy, added to the exclusion list, or in the process of being permanently deleted from Microsoft 365 Backup.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Newly created items are included automatically on subsequent runs.
claims.quote: Newly created artifacts will be included in backup coverage automatically on subsequent runs.

claims.claim: Full Workload Backup can be enabled independently for each of SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange.
claims.quote: You can enable Full Workload Backup independently for SharePoint, OneDrive, and Exchange.

claims.claim: Existing custom backup policies remain unchanged.
claims.quote: Existing custom backup policies will continue to take precedence and remain unchanged.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Custom backup policies take precedence over Full Workload Backup.
claims.quote: Custom backup policies always take precedence over Full Workload Backup.

claims.claim: A custom policy excludes its items from Full Workload Backup whether the custom policy is active or paused.
claims.quote: A protection unit that's already included in a custom backup policy (in an active or paused state) will not be protected by the Full Workload Backup policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Adding a Full Workload Backup item to a custom policy automatically moves it to that custom policy.
claims.quote: If you attempt to add a protection unit that is already protected by Full Workload Backup to a custom backup policy, the protection unit will be moved to that custom policy automatically, with no gap in its recovery point coverage.

claims.claim: That move to a custom policy leaves no gap in recovery point coverage.
claims.quote: the protection unit will be moved to that custom policy automatically, with no gap in its recovery point coverage

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Full Workload Backup is admin-opt-in: it is available by default but protects nothing through this feature until an administrator configures the policy.
claims.quote: The feature is available by default but requires admin configuration to enable.

claims.claim: Microsoft asks for no immediate action before rollout.
claims.quote: No immediate action is required before rollout.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing existing policies and coverage after rollout.
claims.quote:
After rollout, we recommend that you:

- Review your current Microsoft 365 Backup policies and coverage.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends informing backup administrators about the capability.
claims.quote: Inform backup administrators about this new capability.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating internal backup procedure documentation.
claims.quote: Update internal documentation if you manage backup procedures.

claims.claim: The notice identifies administrators managing Microsoft 365 Backup policies as an affected group.
claims.quote:
Who is affected:

- Admins managing Microsoft 365 Backup policies

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup uses a pay-as-you-go consumption model.
claims.quote: The Microsoft 365 Backup service, offered through the Microsoft 365 admin center, is a pay-as-you-go consumption-based service.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The list price is $0.15/GiB/month of protected content.
claims.quote: The list price is $0.15/GiB/month of protected content.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Setup requires linking an Azure subscription for pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: As a first step, you should link an Azure subscription in pay-as-you-go, if you haven't already done so.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The pricing page lists no separate Full Workload Backup charge or meter.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup Full Workload Backup pricing license. Opened backup-pricing and backup-view-edit-policies; pricing gives the general protected-content meter, with no separate Full Workload Backup charge.

claims.claim: The pricing page names no Microsoft 365 licence for the service.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup Full Workload Backup pricing license. Read backup-pricing in full: it names no Microsoft 365 licence. This is a statement about that page, not a claim that billing setup has no licence prerequisite.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Consumption charges are based on the size of content added to backup protection.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Backup charges you based on the size of the following content once it's added to backup protection.

claims.claim: Billable protected storage includes SharePoint and OneDrive second-stage recycle bin content.
claims.quote: Deleted content in SharePoint sites' and OneDrive accounts' second-stage recycle bin (also known as site collection recycle bin).

claims.claim: Billable mailbox storage includes associated online archives when used.
claims.quote: Size of the live user or shared mailbox plus their associated online archives if those are being used.

claims.claim: Billable mailbox storage includes deleted and versioned items held in backup.
claims.quote: Deleted and versioned items in the protected mailboxes.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The linked Microsoft 365 Backup calculator estimates backup storage and cost.
claims.quote: The Microsoft 365 Backup pricing calculator is a tool that helps you estimate the amount of backup storage and the costs that you incur to protect and back up your Microsoft 365 data.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Usage reports or PowerShell can supply size data for the pricing estimate.
claims.quote:
Sizes of live data, and deleted data for your SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts, and Exchange mailboxes can be calculated using two different methods:

- PowerShell commands or scripts
- Microsoft 365 admin center usage reports

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go budgets are set at billing-policy level.
claims.quote: You can only set budgets at the billing policy level, not for individual users, agents, or sites.

claims.claim: Reaching 100% of a budget does not stop service or billing.
claims.quote: Reaching 100% of your budget doesn't stop the service or billing.

claims.claim: The cited billing page says the only way to stop billing is to disconnect the payment method.
claims.quote: The only way to stop billing is to disconnect the payment method.

claims.claim: Customers using an ISV application on the Backup Storage platform are charged solely by that partner for its application.
claims.quote: If you're using a partner (ISV) solution built on the Microsoft 365 Backup Storage platform, you'll be charged solely by them for their application.

claims.claim: Existing backups of excluded or removed items remain available according to retention settings.
claims.quote: Your existing backups stay available for restore based on your retention settings, and you can add the protection unit to any other backup policy.

claims.claim: Only tenant-level administrators can create and manage Microsoft 365 backups.
claims.quote: Only tenant-level admins can create and manage backups using Microsoft 365 Backup for their users.

claims.claim: An administrator's role determines which backup workloads they can manage.
claims.quote: It's important to note that your admin role determines which products you can manage with Microsoft 365 Backup.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Backup Administrator role can manage the entire tool and all three workloads.
claims.quote: We have also introduced a new dedicated role for this tool, the Microsoft 365 Backup Administrator, that can control the entire tool.

claims.quote:

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| SharePoint Administrator | ✓ | ✓ |  |

claims.claim: Global Administrators can manage all three backup workloads.
claims.quote:
| Admin role | OneDrive | SharePoint | Exchange |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Global Administrator | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

claims.claim: Removing protection units from backup policies is listed as a potentially harmful notification event.
claims.quote:
#### Potentially harmful events

- Disabling Microsoft 365 Backup
- Pausing billing due to issues or admin action
- Removing protection units from backup policies

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance; controls[2].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Creating or modifying backup policies is a routine notification event.
claims.quote:
#### Routine events

- Creating or modifying backup policies
- Initiating or completing restores

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance; controls[2].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Routine event notifications require opt-in.
claims.quote: By default, recipients are notified only about potentially harmful events, but you can also opt in to receive notifications for routine events.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The setup page does not explicitly say whether Full Workload Backup exclusion-list edits send email notifications.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup Full Workload Backup notifications exclusion. Opened backup-setup and backup-view-edit-policies. Setup lists general removal and policy-change events but does not identify exclusion-list edits explicitly.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The setup page does not explicitly say whether turning off Full Workload Backup sends an email notification.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup Full Workload Backup exclusion list turn off email notifications separate price license Exchange back up all. Read backup-setup notifications and backup-view-edit-policies shutdown steps; neither explicitly maps this shutdown to an email event.

claims.claim: Removing an item from Full Workload Backup adds it to the policy's exclusion list.
claims.quote: When you remove a protection unit from the Full Workload Backup policy, it's added to the policy's exclusion list.

claims.claim: Removal from Full Workload Backup stops new backups for that item.
claims.quote: This keeps Full Workload Backup from automatically re-protecting it again, and no new backups are taken for it.

claims.claim: Turning off Full Workload Backup removes its policy.
claims.quote:
After Full Workload Backup is turned off:

- The Full Workload Backup policy is removed.

claims.claim: Items protected only by the turned-off policy move to the Removed items tab.
claims.quote: Protection units associated only with the Full Workload Backup policy move to the Removed items tab.

claims.claim: Those removed items receive no new backups until added to a custom policy or Full Workload Backup is re-enabled.
claims.quote: New backups will not be taken, unless and until the protection unit(s) are added to a custom policy or the Full Workload Backup policy is re-enabled.

claims.claim: The Exchange policy creation steps support user and shared mailboxes.
claims.quote: On the Choose selection method page, you can select shared or user mailboxes using any of the available methods.

claims.claim: Room mailboxes are not supported in the documented Exchange creation steps.
claims.quote: Other Exchange recipient types, such as room and group mailboxes, are not supported at this time.

claims.claim: Group mailboxes are not supported in the documented Exchange creation steps.
claims.quote: Other Exchange recipient types, such as room and group mailboxes, are not supported at this time.

claims.claim: Some legacy SharePoint site templates are unsupported.
claims.quote: Some legacy SharePoint site templates are not supported by Microsoft 365 Backup.

claims.claim: Learn documents a limit of 100 backup policies per product.
claims.quote: You can create more than one backup policy for each product (SharePoint, Exchange, and OneDrive) with a limit of 100 policies per product

claims.claim: Learn documents up to 100,000 items per backup policy.
claims.quote: each backup policy can protect up to 100,000 items

claims.claim: The notification setup permits adding another administrator as a user in the Backup Notification List.
claims.quote: Add users, distribution lists, or security groups (only email enabled) to the Backup Notification List.

claims.claim: The notification configuration includes a checkbox for routine event notifications.
claims.quote: (Optional) Select the checkbox to also receive routine event notifications.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Jobs configured with a 10-minute RPO are excluded from notification events.
claims.quote: Jobs configured with a 10-minute RPO are not included in notification events.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Notification events trigger on overall policy completion.
claims.quote: Notification events are triggered upon completion of the overall policy.

claims.claim: Uploading the exclusion CSV is optional on the Exclude sites page during policy creation.
claims.quote:
On the Exclude sites page, select No if you want to protect all SharePoint sites. If you want to exclude specific sites from protection, continue to the next step.
4. (Optional) Upload a CSV file to exclude specific sites from Full Workload Backup protection.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice instructs administrators to review the coverage summary before confirming policy creation.
claims.quote: Review the coverage summary and confirm to create the Full Workload Backup policy.

claims.claim: With Full Workload Backup active, removing an item from a custom policy offers Add to exclusion list or Move to Full Workload Backup.
claims.quote:
When Full Workload Backup is active and you remove a protection unit from a custom backup policy, choose one of the following options:

- Add to exclusion list

claims.claim: Choosing Move to Full Workload Backup transfers the removed custom-policy item into Full Workload Backup on its next run.
claims.quote: Move to Full Workload Backup – The protection unit is removed from the custom backup policy and added to the Full Workload Backup policy in its next run.

claims.claim: The SharePoint creation entry point is Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup > Back up sites > All sites.
claims.quote:
Select Settings.
3. Select Microsoft 365 Backup from the list of products.
On Microsoft 365 Backup dashboard, select Back up sites, and then choose All sites.

claims.claim: New-MgBetaSolutionBackupRestoreSharePointProtectionPolicy -DisplayName '<policy-name>' -ProtectionMode fullServiceBackup creates a SharePoint full-workload policy.
claims.quote:
New-MgBetaSolutionBackupRestoreSharePointProtectionPolicy
    [-ResponseHeadersVariable <string>]
    [-AdditionalProperties <hashtable>]
[-DisplayName <string>]
[-ProtectionMode <string>]

claims.claim: The SharePoint policy creation cmdlet creates an inactive policy rather than activating it.
claims.quote: Create a protection policy for a M365 service SharePoint. Policy will be created in inactive state.

claims.claim: The beta SharePoint protection policy resource defines fullServiceBackup as the protectionMode value for backing up the entire workload.
claims.quote: When set to fullServiceBackup, the entire workload is backed up and specific sites can be excluded using exclusion units.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The exclusion route is Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup > Backup policies > Full Workload Backup policy > View details > Excluded > Exclude more > CSV upload.
claims.quote:
Select the Full Workload Backup policy for the workload, and then select View details.
3. Open the Excluded tab.
4. Select Exclude more.
5. Upload a CSV file containing the protection units that you want to exclude.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/solutions/backupRestore/sharePointProtectionPolicies/{sharePointProtectionPolicyId}/siteExclusionUnitsBulkAdditionJobs creates a SharePoint exclusion job.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/solutions/backupRestore/sharePointProtectionPolicies/845457dc-4bb2-4815-bef3-8628ebd1952e/siteExclusionUnitsBulkAdditionJobs

claims.claim: The exclusion limit is 10,000 protection units per operation.
claims.quote: You can exclude up to 10,000 protection units in a single operation.

claims.claim: The exclusion Graph call requires BackupRestore-Configuration.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote:
| Delegated (work or school account) | BackupRestore-Configuration.ReadWrite.All | Not available. |
| Delegated (personal Microsoft account) | Not supported. | Not supported. |
| Application | BackupRestore-Configuration.ReadWrite.All | Not available. |

claims.claim: The beta exclusion job body sets displayName and siteWebUrls, with siteWebUrls identifying sites to exclude.
claims.quote:
| displayName | String | The display name of the bulk addition job. Required. |
| siteWebUrls | String collection | The URLs of SharePoint sites to be added as exclusion units. Required. |

claims.claim: Email notifications is reached in Microsoft 365 admin center through Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup > Email notifications.
claims.quote:
Select Settings.
3. Select Microsoft 365 Backup from the list of products.
Go to the Email notifications option on the Microsoft 365 Backup home page.

claims.claim: Update-MgSolutionBackupRestoreEmailNotificationSetting -IsEnabled -AdditionalEvents restoreAndPolicyUpdates -Recipients @{Role='custom'; CustomRecipients=@(@{Email='<recipient-email>'})} configures enabled routine notifications and custom recipients.
claims.quote:
[-AdditionalEvents <string>]
[-IsEnabled]
[-Recipients <IMicrosoftGraphNotificationRecipients>]
[CustomRecipients <IMicrosoftGraphEmailIdentity[]>]: A list of users or groups that receive notifications. Only specify this property when role is set to custom.

claims.claim: Global admins and Microsoft 365 Backup admins can enable notifications and update the notification list.
claims.quote: Global admins and Microsoft 365 Backup admins can turn on this feature and update the notification list at any time.

claims.claim: Learn's Full Workload Backup setup example uses SharePoint and says the setup experience is the same for all three workloads.
claims.quote: The setup experience is the same for SharePoint, OneDrive, and Exchange. The following example uses SharePoint.

claims.claim: From Backup policies, administrators select the Full Workload Backup policy and choose Turn off Full Workload Backup to disable it.
claims.quote:
On the Backup policies page, select the Full Workload Backup policy for the workload.
2. Select Turn off Full Workload Backup either from the command bar or the policy details pane.

claims.claim: The Exchange creation steps on Learn do not list a back-up-all option.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup Exchange Back up all. Read backup-view-edit-policies Exchange creation steps: CSV, dynamic rules and filters are listed, but no back-up-all option; the separate Full Workload Backup section says the experience is shared.
